candidate.title: Product Release Cut
candidate.problemStatement: Version labels, manifests, artifacts, signatures, qualification, and channels may each remain valid while participants still lack one exact identity for the qualified product world that is current, installable, or recoverable.
candidate.scope: Provisional product-domain candidate for exact qualified released-world identity; KFD-13 specialization, cross-product transfer, independent adoption, numbering, and universal necessity are not claimed.

observationPerspective.bearer: human and agent participants producing release manifests, channels, artifacts, and evidence
observationPerspective.proximity: inside source, build, signing, qualification, publication, and channel state
consequences: bears release assembly, publication, compatibility, and provenance defects

genesis.observation: Equal-SemVer successors, local dogfood artifacts, public signing, offline installation, and rollback made version and manifest coordinates insufficient as one consequence-bearing product identity.
genesis.candidateObject: Product Release Cut may be an independently addressable root for one exact qualified product world while preserving source, artifact, signing, qualification, platform, and trust-domain authorities.
genesis.claimBoundary: The cut opens qualification and does not decide whether the candidate is an independent Primitive, a KFD-13 Project Cut specialization, a release passport or manifest projection, or no new Primitive.

transformedPerspective.bearer: an installed product, operator, or verifier deciding what exact world is current or recoverable
transformedPerspective.proximity: inside installation, activation, conflict, recovery, and rollback consequences but outside release assembly
consequences: bears wrong-world activation, equal-version conflict, unverifiable recovery, and rollback ambiguity

genesis.transformation: The observer moved from release assembly to the installed participant that must identify exact product reality independently of labels and producer-local state.
genesis.newlyVisibleNeed: One exact product-world identity may be needed across publication, installation, verification, and rollback without absorbing their authorities.
genesis.methodNotes: The existing implementation is evidence for qualification, not proof of minimum closure or independent Primitive identity.

contactSides: release production, publication, and qualification authorities
installed products and operators bearing activation, conflict, recovery, and rollback consequences
boundaryPressure.implicitHandling: Participants reconstruct product identity from SemVer, channel position, manifest paths, artifact digests, timestamps, and cache state.

pressureChanges.description: Public and local trust domains can contain different publication-eligible product worlds.
An incorrect identity can activate, retain, or roll back the wrong product world.

observedFailures: Equal SemVer does not prove identical product reality.
A mutable source cache cannot remain installed identity or rollback authority.
Separate platform artifacts can drift from the intended product-world composition.
Local dogfood evidence may be mistaken for public release qualification.
boundaryPressure.mediationClaim: A Product Release Cut may bind one exact product world while preserving every contributing authority and trust domain.
boundaryPressure.internalObjectAlternative: A KFD-13 Project Cut Domain Profile, release passport, manifest, or SemVer plus artifact digest may provide equivalent identity at lower ontology cost.

pressure: Equal-SemVer worlds may be identical, valid successors, or conflicts.
Public and local trust domains have different publication authority.
Installed identity and rollback must survive source-cache loss.
Platform slices must remain bound to one exact product composition.
grounding.evidenceBoundary: The cut records one founding-adopter executable contract and public architecture at one exact Git cut. It contains no independent adopter, completed comparative deletion test, cross-product transfer, or proof that Project Cut and release-passport alternatives are insufficient.
knownGaps: No completed public and local campaign comparison
No decision between Primitive, Project Cut specialization, manifest, and no-new-Primitive outcomes

alternatives.name: KFD-13 Project Cut specialization
alternatives.reason: A product release may be one software-project settlement profile with installed-product fields rather than a new Primitive.

alternatives.name: Release passport or manifest
alternatives.reason: Existing evidence containers may already bind exact product identity if their roots and trust domains remain immutable.

alternatives.name: SemVer plus artifact digest
alternatives.reason: Systems with immutable version-to-artifact mapping may need no additional identity.

alternatives.name: No new Primitive
alternatives.reason: Product Release Cut may remain Kungfu Profile vocabulary if deletion changes no decision outside the implementation.

contractModel.identity: One content-addressed root over a declared Product Release Cut preimage.
contractModel.boundary: Exact product composition and platform slices, excluding source, artifact, signing, qualification, and participant authorities.
contractModel.authority: May identify one product world; may not authorize movement, certify inputs, publish, install, activate, or roll back it.
contractModel.lifecycle: Proposed, assembled, qualified, published or local-only, installed, active, retained for recovery, or superseded without root mutation.

minimumClosure.notes: The contract closes one implementation but Project Cut and manifest alternatives have not been held fixed and compared.

deletion.notes: Equal-version and recovery pressure is explicit; consequential reconstruction cost has not been measured.

fuse.notes: Fusion with Project Cut, release passport, manifest, and SemVer remains unresolved.

falsifiers: A Project Cut Domain Profile preserves every identity decision at lower ontology cost.
Immutable SemVer-to-artifact mapping makes equal-version conflict and reconstruction impossible.
The Release Cut root adds no decision-relevant information beyond an existing manifest or passport root.
Independent adopters do not reproduce the identity problem.

dogfood.notes: A public implementation witness exists, but comparative KFD-5 qualification and independent review have not run.

decision.reason: Exact product-world identity is operationally explicit and analytically distinguishable, but minimum closure against Project Cut, passport, manifest, SemVer, and no-new-Primitive alternatives remains unproved.
residualRisks: Product terminology may be mistaken for a universal Primitive.
The candidate may duplicate KFD-13 Project Cut.
One implementation may overfit the candidate boundary.
A root aggregate may hide rather than preserve contributing authority.
